maya: Quick follow-up from the onboarding RFC thread. I'm leaning toward splitting ingestion and smoke validation into two decoupled services: ingest (fast, metadata-only) and fast-smoke (behavior + perf). Need feedback on which checks must be deterministic at ingest vs deferred.

javier: prefer ingest = cheap deterministic sanity (manifest, header parse, signature). fast-smoke = behavioral + perf. Otherwise ingest becomes a long job.

sasha: We need a shared contract for checks so teams know what to expect. If ingest and fast-smoke diverge we'll get flaky "works locally, fails in smoke" issues.

lin: Proposed manifest surface (cheap checks only):
```
{"name":"string","tokenizer":{"type":"hf","version":"1.2.0"},"shapes":"{layers:int,hidden:int}","requires_live_load":"bool"}
```
Ingest runs header parse + tokenizer lookup + signature match. Any model with requires_live_load=true gets flagged for synchronous fast-smoke.

maya: For quant/adapter variants: attach variant descriptors to manifest instead of duplicating heavy validation. Base model must pass full checks; variants get a micro-runtime-check using cached golden inputs.

javier: sampling idea: deterministic ingest checks on every push; fast-smoke scheduling uses priority + probabilistic deep-bench gating. PLG/high-traffic models get more deep-bench runs.

sasha: Agree. Also add an "estimated_cost" field returned by ingest so teams see expected GPU-mins for fast-smoke/deep-bench. Reduces surprise.

bench-bot: scheduled fast-smoke job 9421 (trigger: ingest-4932223333)

lin: Artifacts from fast-smoke must include manifest, runtime env (torch/cuda), seed, golden_inputs, and a short diff-summary. Store kernel/quant flags to reproduce regressions.

maya: Owner mapping: ingest team owns manifest validation; smoke team owns behavioral tests; platform owns scheduling + sampling policy. I'll write an addendum mapping failures to owners.

javier: RBAC: mark requires_live_load models as "owner-approve" in ingest response to avoid accidental slow accepts.

sasha: For edge-case tokenizers (model-built vocabs), set requires_live_load=true and optionally run a lightweight tokenization roundtrip test in ingest if possible.

lin: Next actions: I'll draft manifest JSON schema + example. javier will draft sampling policy knobs (probability, priority tiers, cost caps). sasha will enumerate failure categories and owners. maya will author the RFC addendum.

maya: Thanks. If folks agree I'll open the addendum PR today. :thumbsup:
